doc.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001

title: Cannonball Adderley, Louis Hayes, and not caring for the Beatles
summary: He saw Cannonball's band c. 1960-61, interviewed Louis Hayes; indifferent to Lennon, he was fed by Harold Davison's tours of American bands.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: Spoken to him once, saw the band in its heyday, they were in Britain about 60, 61, you know with Nat. And I interviewed Louis Hayes, who was Cannonball’s drummer. And © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-

my great pal came with me to photograph him and we published the story. Louis Hayes was a young man then. We published the story and we published a photograph which was Louis Hayes in his pajamas. Fair enough? He hadn’t got up.
He was in his pajamas. So yes, I was knocked out by Cannonball, no doubt about it.

I mean the Beatles, you know, we are of an age when that was the popular music at the time that my wife and I were married in 1961. And of course, yeah, its kind of music, and I’m not knocking it at all, I don’t think we were caught up in it at that sense. Because by then, you know, jazz was part of our lives. We were going to see bands, and we were seeing any American visits, because we had, in that late 50s period right through I suppose to maybe the early 70s, we had a remarkable booking agency called the Harold Davison office. And every month we had a major tour. The Lionel Hampton band came in to do nineteen dates. The next month it’s the Basie band doing nineteen dates. The next month it’s Ellington. The next month it’s Ella Fitzgerald. The next month it’s Jazz at the Phil. So there was so much going on that my jazz interest was being constantly fed and there was so much interest in pursuing those opportunities of pop music, which is something to go to, to dance to, or to enjoy in a social situation. But I certainly wasn’t particularly interested nor am I now to be honest.
